clue.text: Like steeplejack's job, extremely risky

definitions.meaning: a steeplejack works at great height, so the work is perilous up high, read playfully as 'high-ly'

explanation.surface: A remark that a steeplejack's work is a perilous business.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is a pun: a steeplejack's job is dangerous because it is done high up.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses mean very perilous; the first adds a pun on working at a great height.

clue.text: Fire the lady's shrub!

parts.note: fire gives off heat, and the two words can stand for each other
her is the possessive for a lady

explanation.surface: An exclamation urging someone to set a woman's bush alight.
explanation.definitionFit: Ling, the purple-flowered moorland plant, is a low evergreen bush.

clue.text: Heartless guy went round edge that's dirty

indicators.note: the shortened word goes round the outside of the other piece
taking the heart out of a word removes its middle letter

parts.note: taken as written
a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: A man without feeling circled a grubby border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' looks like an unkind description of the man but strips out his middle letter; 'went round' means the shortened name surrounds the edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Grubby and covered in grime, so soiled.

clue.text: Covering a great distance well into the future

definitions.meaning: said of missiles, flights or guns that reach far
said of forecasts or plans that look far ahead

explanation.surface: Something that spans a vast distance and reaches far ahead in time.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes reach over far space, as in a missile, and far time, as in a weather forecast.

clue.text: Not utter expression of surprise

definitions.meaning: a command to keep quiet, do not speak
an exclamation like 'you don't mean it!'

explanation.surface: Advice to keep quiet about something astonishing.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the phrase forbids speaking; as an exclamation it shows astonishment, like 'Really?'

clue.text: Fidgety reverend shortly absorbed by commonsense in a jumpy state

indicators.note: one piece is taken into the middle of the other

parts.note: nous is informal British for practical good sense

indicators.note: restless and twitchy, so these letters are jiggled into a new order

parts.note: Rev is the short form of Reverend

explanation.surface: A restless clergyman, swallowed up by good sense, is jittery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fidgety' reads as the surface's restless clergyman but signals the shuffle; 'absorbed by' puts the shuffled short title into the British word for common sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Anxious and on edge, as someone easily startled is.

clue.text: Do better taking 90 fish out

indicators.note: one piece takes the other into itself, holding it inside

parts.note: an eel is a snake-like fish
XC is 90 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: An angler outdoes others by landing ninety fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' means the fish holds the numeral inside it; 'out' only completes the angling picture of fishing them out.
explanation.definitionFit: To surpass or outshine others is to be superior.

clue.text: Sociable society expenditure

parts.note: outgoing describes a friendly, extrovert person

explanation.surface: Money spent on lavish social events by the well-connected.
explanation.definitionFit: Money paid out, as a household's spending or costs.

clue.text: Sarah gave trouble during rescue at sea

parts.note: Sal is a pet form of the name Sarah

indicators.note: letters put to trouble are disturbed, so their order is shaken up

explanation.surface: A woman named Sarah caused difficulty while a ship was being saved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' is the verb signalling the shuffle of 'gave'; 'during' simply links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The rescue of a ship or its cargo from loss, a maritime term.

clue.text: In van go round city

indicators.note: turned round, so the letters of the three words are reordered

explanation.surface: Instructions to drive around a town in a van.
explanation.definitionFit: The French city on the Rhône, once seat of the popes.

clue.text: Many an article in genuine performance

indicators.note: the two short pieces go inside the longer word

parts.note: real means true or genuine
C is the Roman numeral for 100, a large number
it can mean a thing or item, an article

explanation.surface: Lots of items in a real show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the insertion; 'an article' looks grammatical, like 'a' or 'the', but means a thing, an item.
explanation.definitionFit: A concert given by a soloist or small group is a musical show.

clue.text: Words to conjure with

parts.note: a famous name is a 'name to conjure with'; here the words are literally said by a conjuror performing a trick

explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation a magician utters as the trick is revealed, a magic formula.

clue.text: Brush footballers found behind toilet

indicators.note: the second piece is placed after the first in the answer

parts.note: loo is British slang for a toilet
FA, the Football Association, governs English football

explanation.surface: A broom discovered by players behind the lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: A bath sponge made of a dried gourd, used to scrub the skin, so a scrubber.

clue.text: State during monarch's incapacity

parts.note: describes the condition of rule by a deputy while a king or queen cannot govern

explanation.definitionFit: Government by a stand-in ruler when the sovereign is a child, ill or absent, as in Britain 1811-20.

clue.text: Mob find weightless sea-organisms on temporary bridge

parts.note: a gang is a mob or crowd

indicators.note: without its weight, so a unit of weight, the ton, is removed

parts.note: plankton are tiny drifting creatures of the sea

explanation.surface: A crowd discovers drifting sea-creatures on a walkway to a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weightless' removes TON, a unit of weight, from PLANKTON, leaving PLANK.
explanation.definitionFit: A movable plank used for boarding or leaving a boat, a portable walkway.

clue.text: Not a sound was heard when license (sic) was removed

indicators.note: read as 're-moved', moved again, so the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Nobody spoke when a misspelt permit was taken away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was removed' reads as re-moved, shifting the letters of LICENSE; '(sic)' admits that is the American spelling of the British noun licence.
explanation.definitionFit: Total quiet is the absence of any noise.

clue.text: Pale yellow spot on sweet

parts.note: lemon is a pale yellow colour
a drop is a spot of liquid

explanation.surface: A small pale yellow mark on a dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' just joins the pieces in a down clue, the first written above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard citrus-flavoured boiled candy is a confection.

clue.text: Man's about to regret becoming ballet-dancer

parts.note: Dan is a man's name, and 's adds the S

indicators.note: turned about, so the word for regret is read backwards

parts.note: to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: A fellow is going to be sorry about becoming a dancer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the turnaround; the ballet term is French, the male form of danseuse.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for a male ballet performer, the masculine counterpart of a ballerina.

clue.text: Watch after one's come off drug

indicators.note: these letters are detached from the end of the longer word

parts.note: digitalis is a heart drug made from foxglove
one is I, and 's adds S

explanation.surface: A timepiece check once someone has quit a drug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'come off' takes IS (one's, I plus S) from the end of DIGITALIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A digital timepiece shows the time in numerals, so the word describes a type of wristwatch.

clue.text: Reshape remainder you once left inside

parts.note: the rest is what remains

indicators.note: the letter for left goes into the middle of the old word for you

parts.note: ye is an archaic word for you

explanation.surface: Remould what remains, with an old 'you' and a left turn tucked in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' places the abbreviation for left within the archaic pronoun, which follows the word for what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: To redesign the look of something, such as hair, is to alter its form.

clue.text: One of nine in rose's place puzzled

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a rose grows in a flower bed
the Muses of Greek myth were nine sisters

explanation.surface: A flower lover is baffled by where a rose belongs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One of nine' looks like a count but refers to the nine Muses.
explanation.definitionFit: Bewildered or confused is the sense of being at a loss.

clue.text: See city of fashion

definitions.meaning: a bishop's diocese; the Church of England has one centred on this city
the phrase 'shipshape and ... fashion' means in good order

explanation.surface: An invitation to visit a stylish town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is not a command but a noun, a bishop's seat; 'shipshape and Bristol fashion' is a British idiom for neat and orderly.
explanation.definitionFit: The English port is a cathedral seat of a diocese and gives its name to the idiom about tidiness.

clue.text: Lower inside pressurised container

indicators.note: the words contain the answer, which runs across them

explanation.surface: Drop the level inside a pressure vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'container' signals the run across the end of 'inside' and the start of 'pressurised'.
explanation.definitionFit: To push down or reduce is to bring something down.

clue.text: One staring at space hesitantly

parts.note: a gap is a space
er is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: Someone gazing uncertainly into the void.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who gapes stares open-mouthed.

clue.text: Egg found in new sort of resting-place

indicators.note: one piece is discovered within the other
made new, so the letters of the word are rearranged

parts.note: O is egg-shaped, so it can stand for an egg

explanation.surface: An egg is discovered in a novel kind of nest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges SORT into ROST; 'found in' puts O inside it after R.
explanation.definitionFit: A perch where birds settle for the night is a place to sleep.

clue.text: Bathe naked in north America

parts.note: describes the North American informal phrase for swimming without clothes

explanation.definitionFit: The informal term, originally American, for swimming nude.

clue.text: Day before poet appeared

parts.note: ante is Latin for before

explanation.surface: A poet showed up a day early.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian author of the Divine Comedy is a great writer of verse.

clue.text: It keeps hot pot for reverend Spooner

annotationWithheld.why: It keeps hot pot for reverend Spooner (3,4): a cryptic definition whose Spoonerism turns the definition itself ('pot hot' said as 'hot pot'), not letters of the answer; spoon() must build TEACOSY, so the device cannot be expressed and a plain cd is refused as losing the Spoonerism
annotationWithheld.clue: It keeps hot pot for reverend Spooner

clue.text: Man uprooted tree going round small enclosure

indicators.note: the rearranged word goes round the other piece
pulled up and disturbed, so the letters of the word are rearranged

parts.note: enc is the short form of enclosure

explanation.surface: A fellow pulled up a tree that grew around a little pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprooted' signals the shuffle of 'tree'; 'going round' wraps it around the abbreviation. Terence was a Roman comic playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: A male first name, as of the Roman playwright, so a man.

clue.text: Appreciate those applauding when going very quickly

parts.note: to like something is to appreciate it
the people clapping are the clappers

explanation.surface: Enjoy the audience's applause as it races along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like the clappers' is British slang for at great speed.
explanation.definitionFit: A British idiom meaning extremely fast, at full pelt.
